findings.title: State-dependent salience

findings.mechanism: 29:64 frames ordinary life as distracting occupation and aimless action; 29:65 sequences exclusive devotion under danger, rescue, and renewed association, returning through focus beautification and the state verb.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees a possible state-sensitive switch in what governs action, rather than a stable absence or presence of insight.
findings.containment: All HFT context branches are unresolved except the supplied focus beautification, state, and path-related branch. The psychological state-switch is an inference, with simple rhetorical inconsistency retained as an alternative.

epistemic.reason: All HFT context branches are unresolved except the supplied focus beautification, state, and path-related branch. The psychological state-switch is an inference, with simple rhetorical inconsistency retained as an alternative.
